analysis.one_liner: ONGC is India's largest oil and gas exploration and production company, a government-controlled PSU that extracts crude oil and natural gas domestically and holds stakes in refining/petrochemical arms like MRPL, HPCL and OPaL.
analysis.whats_happening: Crude prices spiked through 2026 on Middle East tensions, pushing ONGC's Q1 FY27 (June quarter) standalone profit up 112% YoY to a record Rs 17,034 crore on realizations of $99.45/barrel. Yet the stock sits at a 52-week low, down 27% from its August 2024 peak, as windfall taxes on crude have been reinstated and consolidated group profit is being dragged down by losses at refining subsidiary HPCL. Q2 FY27 results are expected in early-to-mid November 2026 (exact board meeting date not yet announced) and will show whether these elevated realizations held through the September quarter.
analysis.plain_terms: ONGC pumps crude oil and natural gas out of the ground and sells it, mostly to domestic refiners, so its profit swings with global oil prices - when oil is expensive, it earns more on every barrel. Right now oil is expensive due to Middle East tensions, which doubled ONGC's standalone profit versus last year, but the government also raises windfall taxes when crude prices rise, clawing back part of that extra profit directly from the company. The stock sitting near its 52-week low despite record profit captures this tension: the market may be pricing in either a pullback in crude or further tax hikes, and the group's reported consolidated earnings look far weaker than standalone because loss-making refiner HPCL offsets ONGC's own numbers. Separate "how much crude oil is worth" (ONGC's upside) from "how much tax or subsidiary losses eat into that" (what is capping the stock) before drawing conclusions.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter) standalone revenue was Rs 46,460 crore, up 45% YoY, with PBT of Rs 22,848 crore - the highest quarterly PBT on record - and PAT of Rs 17,034 crore, up 112% YoY, driven almost entirely by average crude realization rising to $99.45/barrel. Consolidated figures are messier and conflict across sources: one tracker shows consolidated PAT falling 52% QoQ to Rs 6,554 crore, another shows it up 21% YoY to Rs 11,899 crore. The gap traces to a roughly Rs 12,265 crore net loss at refining subsidiary HPCL (fuel under-recoveries during the crude spike) dragging down the group total - treat the standalone Rs 17,034 crore figure as the more reliable number and the consolidated PAT as unresolved pending ONGC's own filing. Management guided FY27 capex at $3.5-4 billion and noted new wells now contribute 19% of gas volume. Q2 FY27 results are expected in the first half of November 2026.
analysis.performance_read: There is no recent corporate action distorting the chart - ONGC's last stock split was in 2016 - so the current 27% drawdown from the August 2024 peak of Rs 306.57 to today's Rs 223.94 is a genuine price decline, not an artifact. Despite that, longer-run returns are strong relative to peers: ONGC is up 39.8% over 3 years and 86.6% over 5 years, well ahead of the Nifty (15.9%/23.7%) and far ahead of peer Reliance (2.6%/-3.1%). The 1-year return of -4.8% actually beats both the Nifty (-9.7%) and Reliance (-13.2%), so the stock has underperformed its own recent high but not the broader market. It sits at its 52-week low today.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 6.4-6.5x and P/B of 0.76x, ONGC trades well below its long-term historical average P/E of around 8-10x and below book value - cheap on the surface. Why it's cheap: PSU oil and gas stocks are structurally discounted for government control (capex and dividend decisions can serve policy goals over shareholder returns), exposure to windfall taxes that cap upside when crude rallies, and dependence on volatile global crude prices rather than a predictable business model. Whether it is actually cheap depends on whether the current high realizations ($99.45/barrel) persist - if these are a cyclical peak, today's low P/E is being calculated on an unsustainably high earnings base and could look less cheap once realizations normalize.
analysis.growth_read: This quarter's growth was overwhelmingly price-led, not volume-led - the 45% YoY revenue jump and 112% YoY profit jump trace to a higher crude realization per barrel, not to ONGC extracting materially more oil or gas. Management did flag that new wells now supply 19% of gas volumes, pointing to some underlying production additions, but the headline growth is a price story, which is inherently less durable than volume growth - if crude prices retreat, this growth reverses mechanically regardless of operational execution.
analysis.health_read: ROE of roughly 11.6-12.7% and ROCE of 11.5-14.2% are respectable for a capital-intensive PSU, and debt has not surfaced as a concern in available data, though debt-to-equity could not be independently verified - check on Screener. The more relevant risk here is business risk, not financial risk: profits are tied to global crude prices and to government windfall-tax policy, both outside the company's control, and the consolidated numbers show that losses at refining subsidiary HPCL (around Rs 12,265 crore in the June quarter) can meaningfully offset ONGC's own strong standalone cash generation at the group level.
analysis.ownership_read: The Government of India remains the dominant promoter at roughly 58.89%, with no pledging reported - expected for a PSU, since government-held shares are not pledged. Domestic institutions hold about 19.3% and foreign institutional investors about 8%, with retail and others making up the remaining free float of roughly 3-3.5%. There is no well-known individual investor on the register; this is a government-controlled, institution-heavy shareholding base rather than one anchored by a famous name.
strengths: Standalone PAT of Rs 17,034 crore in Q1 FY27, up 112% YoY, with the highest-ever quarterly PBT of Rs 22,848 crore
Dividend yield of 5.92% (TTM dividend Rs 13.25/share), among the highest in the large-cap space
5-year return of 86.6% has beaten both the Nifty (23.7%) and peer Reliance (-3.1%)
AAA/A1+ credit rating reaffirmed as recently as October 9, 2026
watchpoints: Consolidated PAT figures conflict sharply across sources (Rs 6,554 crore vs Rs 11,899 crore) due to a roughly Rs 12,265 crore loss at HPCL - the group number is far less clean than the standalone number
Windfall tax (SAED) was reinstated in March 2026 and revised again in July 2026, meaning policy can claw back a chunk of any crude-price upside at short notice
Stock is at its 52-week low and down 27% from its August 2024 peak despite record standalone profit, suggesting the market is treating current earnings as cyclically elevated
Debt-to-equity could not be verified from available sources - confirm balance-sheet leverage directly before drawing conclusions on financial risk
analysis.one_thing: Whether average crude oil realization holds near the $99.45/barrel seen in Q1 FY27 through the Q2 FY27 results (expected early-to-mid November 2026) - that number determines whether this quarter's 112% profit jump is a new earnings level or a cyclical peak.
analysis.data_notes: Standalone Q1 FY27 figures (revenue, PBT, PAT, crude realization) were cross-checked across IndianPSU, ApacNewsNetwork and ONGC's own earnings transcript. Consolidated PAT conflicts between Screener.in and other trackers due to HPCL losses and could not be resolved - flagged above rather than averaged. Debt-to-equity and the exact Q2 FY27 results date could not be verified and should be checked on Screener/NSE filings. Shareholding percentages are for the June 2026 quarter; September 2026 quarter data was not yet published at time of writing.
